question:
A 26-year-old male medical student visits the school clinic with complaints of mild chest pain and
mid-back pain. The symptoms began 3 days ago after he increased his daily study time to prepare for
an upcoming cardiovascular exam. He describes the back pain as constant, sharp, and achy, and
notes that the chest pain occurs after meals but resolves spontaneously. He has no significant medical
history and takes no medications. Vital signs are normal. On examination, there is a tender, localized
area of tissue congestion on the midline of the sternum at the level of the costal cartilage of rib 5, with
the patient rating the pain as 10/10. Tenderness and hypertonicity are also noted in the paraspinal

muscles from T2–T6. The student doctor begins treatment by positioning the patient supine with his
arms dangling off the table and placing her thigh under the patient’s upper thoracic region. Using her
thigh, she elevates the patient toward the dysfunction while monitoring with her hand, which reduces
the pain to 6/10. What is the next best step to optimize the treatment? Answer Choices: (A) Apply
sustained pressure to the tender point (B) Perform myofascial release to the pectoralis muscles (C)
Forward bend the neck toward the chest (D) Apply counterstrain technique to the affected area (E)
Extend the thoracic spine (F) Apply high-velocity low-amplitude thrust (G) Perform muscle energy
technique to the thoracic region (H) Perform bilateral rib raising technique (I) Back off with the thigh to
lower the patient back toward the table (J) Sidebend thorax to either side for fine-tuning
 A. Apply high-velocity low-amplitude thrust
B. Apply sustained pressure to the tender point
C. Apply counterstrain technique to the affected area
D. Perform bilateral rib raising technique
E. Forward bend the neck toward the chest
F. Perform muscle energy technique to the thoracic region
G. Sidebend thorax to either side for fine-tuning
H. Extend the thoracic spine
I. Back off with the thigh to lower the patient back toward the table
J. Perform myofascial release to the pectoralis muscles
